# ModDotPlot Browser user guide

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

ModDotPlot Browser creates interactive comparative genomic dotplots entirely in a desktop
browser. Your sequence files are processed locally and are not uploaded by the
application.

## Supported browsers

Use a current desktop version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari with WebAssembly,
Web Workers, and WebGL2 enabled. Mobile browsers are not supported in this functional
preview.

The application must be opened from an HTTP or HTTPS address. A downloaded build will
not work reliably by double-clicking `index.html`, because browsers restrict module
workers and WebAssembly on `file://` pages.

## Create a plot

1. Drop one or more plain, gzip-compressed, or BGZF FASTA files on the large FASTA
   target, or use its file chooser. BGZF is detected from its header even when the
   suffix is `.gz`. For indexed loading, include `sample.fa.fai` with `sample.fa`, or
   include both `sample.fa.gz.fai` and `sample.fa.gz.gzi` with a BGZF
   `sample.fa.gz`.
2. Optionally drop BED, GFF, or GTF annotation files on the smaller annotation target
   beneath it, or use that target's file chooser.
3. Wait for the selected files to become viewable, then select the green **Explore**
   button. Eager input reports **Reading and validating** with a percentage while it
   streams, decompresses where needed, validates FASTA, and packs sequence. Indexed
   input validates its metadata without first packing every record. The application
   stays on the launch screen until this explicit step; after it, the workspace opens,
   its DNA helix indicates active work, and the status line reports on-demand sequence
   loading, signature construction, tile drawing, and refinement progress.
   To try the application without choosing local files, select **Try ModDotPlot on an
   *Arabidopsis thaliana* genome**. The initial Chr1 self plot comes from the bundled
   `Col-CEN_v1.2.Chr1.mdp-overview-v1.gz` artifact, an approximately 256 KB compressed,
   refined 1,000-by-1,000 overview. The complete 134 MB FASTA and 3.6 MB annotation do
   not block that first plot. Startup also retrieves the 195-byte FAI and requires it
   to match the artifact exactly. The raw FASTA remains available on the same static
   origin for indexed byte-range requests, and the CEN180 annotation starts in a
   separate load after the workspace opens rather than gating the plot. Static refined
   2,000- and 4,000-cell Chr1 detail matrices cache in the background so the first two
   zoom levels do not require FASTA range reads or browser-side sketch construction.
4. Choose the available sequence or plot mode. A one-record session has one self
   selector. When more than one record is loaded, the Self plot, Pairwise plot, and
   Grid plot tabs appear with Self plot selected initially.
5. Explore immediately when the quick view appears. A higher-accuracy view replaces
   its tiles after the quick viewport has been painted.

### Choose a plot mode

With one loaded record, the mode tabs are hidden and the interface provides one
sequence selector for its self plot. Loading more than one record reveals three tabs
and starts in Self plot:

* **Self plot** provides one sequence selector and compares that record with itself.
* **Pairwise plot** compares two different records in the full interactive plot. It
  selects the first two available records by default. Choosing the record currently
  used on the other axis moves that other axis to a different record automatically,
  preserving a distinct pair while allowing direct X/Y orientation swaps.
* **Grid plot** provides a grid-size control and that many sequence selectors. Choose
  `n` from 2 through `min(6, loaded records)`; all `n` selected records must be
  distinct.

Grid mode computes `n` self comparisons and `n choose 2` unique pairwise comparisons,
one at a time. Each is a quick-only overview bounded to a 512 by 512 matrix, regardless
of the interactive Plot resolution setting. The result is displayed as a complete
`n`-by-`n` symmetric matrix. X labels follow the selected order from left to right; Y
labels follow that same order from bottom to top. Self plots therefore occupy the
bottom-left-to-top-right diagonal. Each unique pairwise plot occupies one side of that
diagonal, and its transposed rendering fills the reciprocal cell with the displayed X/Y
order preserved. Thus the maximum six-sequence grid performs 6 self comparisons plus
15 unique pairwise comparisons, not 36 independent calculations.

Every grid cell uses the longest selected sequence as its common genomic X/Y extent.
That longest record therefore fills its self-comparison cell. A shorter record occupies
only its proportional width or height and the unsupported remainder stays blank: its
self plot is smaller on both axes, while a pairwise plot uses the column record's
proportional width and the row record's proportional height. This common scale keeps
the genomic coordinates aligned across every row, column, self plot, and reciprocal
pairwise plot.

Each X and Y label includes a reorder handle. Drag a handle onto another label to move
that sequence in the shared order; either axis may be used and both axes update
together. A focused X handle can also move with Left/Right, and a focused Y handle with
Down/Up. Reordering rearranges the retained cells and does not rerun their comparisons.

Click a grid cell to open it in the full interactive plot. A diagonal cell opens Self
plot with that sequence selected; an off-diagonal cell opens Pairwise plot with the
cell's sequences on its axes. The interactive comparison includes **Back to grid**,
which restores the existing grid overview and its selections. Grid is an overview, so
feature tracks, **Reset view**, and current-view data/image export are unavailable
until a cell is opened in Self or Pairwise mode.

Completed grid data and canvases are retained while that grid-opened comparison is
active, making **Back to grid** immediate and avoiding recomputation. Choosing another
workflow instead exits the return flow and releases the retained grid resources.

Multiple records and files may be loaded together. Each FASTA record is an independent
axis choice. A single record may contain up to 1,000,000,000 bases, although the total
packed records retained together must fit the 3 GiB Wasm session budget.

Without a usable index set, all records are read and retained eagerly. With a matching
plain FASTA plus `.fai`, or BGZF FASTA plus `.fai` and `.gzi`, record identifiers and
lengths become selectable from the indexes first. A selected Self or Pairwise record,
or each record needed by Grid, is then streamed and packed on demand. Once loaded, that
record stays in the current Wasm session and later comparisons reuse it. Keep indexed
source files available to the tab for the lifetime of the session; the browser's
existing `File` references are the source for a record that has not yet been loaded.

Companion names include the full FASTA filename: `assembly.fa.fai` describes
`assembly.fa`, and `assembly.fa.gz.fai` plus `assembly.fa.gz.gzi` describe
`assembly.fa.gz`. A FAI alone is sufficient only for a plain seekable FASTA. GZI
random access requires BGZF; ordinary single-stream gzip continues through eager
loading. An incomplete optional companion set also falls back to eager loading, while
an orphan `.fai` or `.gzi` with no matching sequence file is rejected.

Generate a plain-FASTA index with:

```bash
samtools faidx assembly.fa
```

This creates `assembly.fa.fai`. To keep the original FASTA, create BGZF plus both
required indexes with `N` replaced by the desired compression thread count:

```bash
bgzip -@ N -k -i assembly.fa
samtools faidx assembly.fa.gz
```

The first command creates `assembly.fa.gz` and `assembly.fa.gz.gzi`; the second creates
`assembly.fa.gz.fai`. Select the FASTA and its matching companion file or files
together in ModDotPlot Browser.

The first whitespace-delimited FASTA header field is the sequence identifier. Header
text after it is the description. Selectors use `SeqID_FileStem · Size` so records such
as `chr1` from two assemblies remain distinct; a numeric suffix is added only if that
combination is still duplicated. Axis labels may show both identifier and description.
FAI metadata contains the identifier but not the optional description, so an indexed
record uses its FAI identifier and source filename for the entire session, including
after the record is loaded. The first time that record is requested, the browser reads
its real FASTA header and verifies that the header identifier matches the FAI before
committing the parsed record. This lazy check uses a bounded 256 KiB lookback before
the indexed first-base offset; a header that cannot be validated within that window,
including an extremely long header beyond the bound, is rejected. BEDPE/CSV sequence
fields use only the FASTA identifier.

Sequence input is handed to Wasm through a reusable bounded 4 MiB ingestion buffer.
Ordinary and indexed record streams share the same FASTA validation and packed-sequence
boundary. The memory indicator combines Wasm, JavaScript tile, GPU texture, annotation,
computed-track, and publication estimates. If a layer exceeds its budget, the
application reports the applicable eviction, lower-detail, sharding, or rejection
fallback. Robust one-billion-base use on ordinary laptops remains conditional on
further measurements.

Upper- and lowercase `U` are accepted and normalized to `T`; they are indistinguishable
after loading. IUPAC ambiguity and gap characters retain their coordinates but prevent
every overlapping k-mer from contributing. Other sequence symbols are rejected.

FASTA and annotation input have separate launch targets. A file dropped on the wrong
target is refused. If any selected sequence file cannot be parsed as FASTA, no partial
sequence set is published; the application remains on the launch screen and reports
the problem in a dialog.

### Bundled example cache and byte ranges

The bundled example's precomputed artifact covers exactly the initial Chr1-versus-Chr1
plot at the default 1,000-cell resolution, 21-mer setting, and 1,024-register refined
configuration. Palette, background, and cursor-guide changes can redraw those cached
numeric tiles without fetching sequence. Changing to another chromosome, opening a
pairwise or grid comparison, requesting an uncached zoom/detail level, entering exact
mode, or enabling a sequence-derived track requires sequence bases and therefore reads
the necessary indexed range from the raw FASTA.

The artifact is not accepted merely because its filename is present. Its compressed
bytes must match the release's pinned SHA-256, and the separately retrieved FAI text
must exactly match the embedded index. Its gzip stream,
versioned header, payload lengths, complete matrix coverage, source manifest, FAI
metadata, tile provenance, configuration digest, and full canonical scientific
configuration identity are validated. The configuration must exactly match one built
by the running Wasm engine; incompatible tiles are never relabeled as current results.

Hosts serving the bundled example must keep the artifact, FASTA, and annotation on the
same origin as the application and support standard HTTP byte ranges for the FASTA.
On the first uncached sequence request, the browser probes the FASTA with a two-byte
request and requires a valid `206 Partial Content` response. A server that ignores
`Range` and replies with the full file is
rejected before that response body is consumed. Later requests also validate
`Content-Range`, total size, content encoding, redirects, and any available ETag or
Last-Modified validator. These same-origin asset requests are visible to the static
hosting provider even though locally selected files remain browser-local.

`ColCEN_CEN180.gff3` is not part of the startup fetch set. Its retrieval and local
parse start separately after the workspace opens and do not gate the precomputed plot.
When ready, its one logical CEN180 row maps automatically to matching chromosomes as
described under Imported annotations.

## Read the plot

In **Similarity** mode, each pixel summarizes one interval on the X axis against one
interval on the Y axis. Color represents the containment-derived ModDotPlot score:

```text
ANI_c = containment^(1/k)
```

`ANI_c` is a display transform of k-mer containment. It is not biological average
nucleotide identity and should not be interpreted as equivalent to alignment-derived
`ANI_m`. The sketch is validated against exact containment from complete canonical
k-mer sets.

Containment is evaluated in both core-versus-expanded directions and the larger value
is displayed. The expansion makes the plot less sensitive to two homologous intervals
falling slightly out of register with the matrix grid.

The default heatmap uses a white plot background below 85% identity and the reversed
11-class Spectral palette through 100%: lower displayed identity begins at purple and
higher identity reaches red. Values above the selected maximum retain the palette's
resolved top color.

The palette menu starts with dedicated Spectral and Viridis groups so those two common
choices remain adjacent. The remaining schemes are drawn from
[ColorBrewer 2](https://colorbrewer2.org/) and grouped as sequential, diverging, and
qualitative; Spectral is omitted from the later Diverging group. Viridis is a separately
sourced application palette rather than a ColorBrewer scheme. Its supported variants
are exact discrete samples from
[d3-scale-chromatic's published 256-color table](https://github.com/d3/d3-scale-chromatic/blob/main/src/sequential-multi/viridis.js),
without RGB interpolation.

After choosing a palette, choose a supported discrete color count; the control's
minimum and maximum update to the sizes defined for that scheme. Every palette supports
at least 3 colors. Viridis reaches 12 colors, sequential palettes reach 9, and the
remaining diverging palettes reach 11. Qualitative maxima vary by scheme as shown below.

| Menu group | Palettes | Supported colors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spectral | Spectral | 3–11 |
| Viridis | Viridis | 3–12 |
| Sequential | Blues, BuGn, BuPu, GnBu, Greens, Greys, Oranges, OrRd, PuBu, PuBuGn, PuRd, Purples, RdPu, Reds, YlGn, YlGnBu, YlOrBr, YlOrRd | 3–9 |
| Diverging | BrBG, PiYG, PRGn, PuOr, RdBu, RdGy, RdYlBu, RdYlGn | 3–11 |
| Qualitative | Accent, Dark2, Pastel2, Set2 | 3–8 |
| Qualitative | Pastel1, Set1 | 3–9 |
| Qualitative | Paired, Set3 | 3–12 |

The compact **Distinct colors** control shares its row with the **Direction**/**Flip**
control. Spectral starts reversed; every other palette starts in its canonical
direction. Flipping reverses the complete ordered class list, including any edited
colors.

One color swatch is shown for each active class. Selecting a swatch opens an editor with
a **Color wheel** control, a six-digit **Hex code** field, and **Reset color**. Activating
the color control uses the browser/operating-system native picker, whose exact wheel or
other interface varies by environment. A change is applied to the interactive plot,
retained grid previews, and image exports. The selected colors are rendered as discrete
identity classes. The identity handles map those classes across the selected range.
Moving them in 0.1 percentage-point increments recolors cached tiles immediately and
does not rerun the sequence calculation. The plot background can be switched between
white and black.
While the plot is empty or loading, its unpainted area remains white. A selected black
background is applied inside plotted tiles only.

In **Direction** mode, forward and reverse matches have distinct colors. Direction
comes from the canonical orientations of verified matching k-mers in both containment
directions. Low-support colors are blended toward gray; this reduces visual confidence
without weakening the underlying match intensity.

Hover over the plot to see the `ANI_c` score and exact X/Y coordinate intervals. Each
interval explicitly starts with its selected sequence name. A self plot therefore
shows the same name for X and Y, while a pairwise plot shows its two different names.
Dotted horizontal and vertical guides cross at the pointer by default, making it easier
to follow the same row or column across the plot. Advanced options can hide this
overlay, change it to crossing diagonals, or use dotted, dashed, or solid strokes. The
guides are display aids only and are omitted from exports. Areas outside a shorter
selected record are blank.

When available horizontal space exceeds the plot's required width, the complete plot
assembly is centered rather than anchored to the control panel.

## Navigate

* Use the mouse wheel or trackpad to zoom around the pointer.
* Drag the plot to pan.
* Select **Reset view** to return to the complete comparison.
* In Self mode, change the single sequence selector to start another self comparison.
* In Pairwise mode, change either sequence selector at any time to start another
  comparison.
* In Grid mode, click a cell to open its interactive self or pairwise comparison.
* From a comparison opened through Grid mode, select **Back to grid** to restore that
  grid overview and its selected records.
* Choosing another workflow instead of **Back to grid** leaves the return flow and
  releases the retained grid overview.

Zooming stops when each displayed axis spans 100 bp; for a sequence shorter than 100
bp, its full shorter extent is the limit. Wheel, keyboard, and programmatic viewport
navigation share this bound, so no interaction can open a view closer than the
available 100-by-100-bp area.

When entering a new level, the existing lower-resolution image is enlarged immediately.
Quick tiles then replace it. Tiles near the active display floor or with weak support,
their immediate neighbors, and a small deterministic exploratory sample receive
detailed estimates if the viewport remains current. Moving elsewhere cancels obsolete
detailed work. The exploratory sample prevents an apparently blank quick region from
being permanently excluded from refinement.

At maximum zoom, exact samples represent individual base pairs rather than approximate
window sketches, while the visible viewport remains at least 100 bp per available
axis. The exact-mode panel reports the one-base cell size, canonical k-mer length,
fixed full-footprint geometry, and coloring semantics. **Bases** is the default exact
view: A green, C blue, G orange, and T red, with its categorical legend titled
**Base**. **Identity** uses the active similarity palette.

Every matching canonical k-mer is painted across its complete footprint from its start
through `start + k - 1`, including the corresponding reverse diagonal for
reverse-complement matches. This geometry is fixed and has no separate control.

Cells without supporting exact k-mer evidence use the selected plot background, as do
valid zero-identity or below-threshold cells. The old gray missing-evidence boxes and
bottom-left exact-state key are not shown. The categorical **Base** legend remains for
interpreting A/C/G/T match colors. The main **Similarity / Direction** control remains
available when orientation coloring is needed.

## Controls

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Self plot / Pairwise plot / Grid plot | Choose the workflow; these tabs appear only when more than one record is loaded |
| Self sequence | Select one FASTA record for a self comparison |
| X sequence / Y sequence | Select two different FASTA records in Pairwise mode; a colliding choice automatically moves the other axis to keep the pair distinct |
| Grid size / Grid sequences | Select 2 through `min(6, loaded records)` distinct records for the overview |
| Grid axis reorder handles | Drag a sequence label, or use its axis arrow keys, to rearrange the shared X/Y order without recomputing |
| Similarity / Direction | Switch coloring without recomputing tiles |
| Exact view: Bases / Identity | At one-base detail, color exact matches by A/C/G/T base or with the active palette; Bases is the default and its legend is titled **Base** |
| Palette | Select Spectral, Viridis, or a ColorBrewer sequential, diverging, or qualitative scheme; Spectral and Viridis appear first |
| Distinct colors | Select a supported discrete class count; minimum 3, with a palette-specific maximum of 8, 9, 11, or 12 |
| Direction / Flip | Reverse the ordered palette colors; Spectral begins flipped and other palettes begin canonical |
| Color swatches | Open an editor with a native color control, editable six-digit hex code, and reset action |
| Identity range | Map the palette's low, midpoint, and high colors from 80% to 100% |
| White / Black background | Choose the color used for the plot and below-minimum cells; white is the default |
| Feature tracks | Enable sequence-derived tracks or import BED/GFF/GTF annotations, optionally gzip compressed |
| Plot window size | Genomic interval represented by each matrix pixel at the current zoom level; hover the question mark for a sentence-form explanation |
| Export ModDotPlot command | Save current-view BEDPE values plus an official-CLI JSON config in one ZIP package |
| Export image | Save the complete current composition as PNG (default), SVG, or PDF |
| Reset view | Return to the full comparison and redraw the overview |
| Back to grid | Return from a grid-opened comparison to the existing grid overview |
| Clear | Remove loaded sequences and cached results |

### Advanced controls

Advanced controls are collapsed by default.

| Control | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Plot resolution | Full-view matrix dimension: 500, 1,000, 2,000, or 4,000 cells per axis |
| Cursor guides | Show or hide the pointer-following overlay; shown by default |
| Guide geometry | Use horizontal/vertical lines or crossing diagonals |
| Guide style | Use dotted (default), dashed, or solid strokes |
| Quick accuracy | Registers used for the first visible estimate; default 256 |
| Detailed accuracy | Registers used for background refinement; default 1,024 |
| K-mer length | Canonical k-mer length used for sketching and terminal exact matching; default 21 |

Plot resolution changes the number of independently calculated matrix cells, not the CSS
size of the plot. The plot expands with the browser window while retaining the selected
scientific resolution. The primary **Plot window size** control translates the current
scientific resolution into genomic coordinates. It updates as the plot zooms and reports one
nearest-whole-base value per cell when the common domain does not divide evenly. Grid
plots report that the value varies until an individual comparison is opened because
their sequence lengths can differ.

Register count controls sampling accuracy and cost. More registers generally reduce
variance but require more construction time, comparison work, and memory. It is not an
exact k-mer sampling percentage because register occupancy varies with sequence length,
complexity, and duplicate k-mers. The quick count cannot exceed the detailed count.

Changing a scientific control invalidates incompatible cached levels and starts a new
quick view without changing the current pan or zoom. For routine navigation, the
defaults are the recommended starting point.
The compact methods line below these controls reports ntHash2, the estimator, register
tiers, HLL precision, and the scientific configuration digest. Hover it for the full
parameter set.

## Export results

Current-view data and image export apply to the interactive Self and Pairwise modes.
They are unavailable in Grid mode because the grid contains multiple bounded quick
overviews rather than one detailed current viewport. Click a grid cell to open its
interactive comparison before exporting.

Select **Export ModDotPlot command** to save one ZIP package containing a BEDPE and its
companion JSON config.
BEDPE writes each nonzero valid current-view cell as an interval pair with `ANI_c`,
relative direction, and support. Configuration and estimator details are kept once in
the provenance preamble rather than repeated in every BEDPE row. Zero-valued and
missing cells are omitted. The exact column definitions and formulas are in
[Data export formats](EXPORT_FORMATS.md).

Extract `<plot-name>.bedpe` and `<plot-name>.config.json` into the same directory. The
config already contains `"load": ["./<plot-name>.bedpe"]`; run it with
`moddotplot -c <plot-name>.config.json -l <plot-name>.bedpe` using the official
ModDotPlot develop version.
The config carries the selected records and visible regions, k-mer and window settings,
identity thresholds, exact ordered colors, direction coloring, and pairwise/grid layout.
ModDotPlot Browser and the official CLI use different estimators, so the JSON recreates
the view and recomputes it with the publication CLI; it does not promise byte-identical
browser cell values. The CLI requires a window of at least 10 bp and one k-mer, so an
export made below that scale records the browser's requested cell size in
`_moddotplot_browser.requested_bp_per_cell` and uses the smallest runnable CLI window.

Before either data or image output is written, every tile intersecting the current view
is calculated with the selected **Detailed accuracy** register count. Terminal zoom is
exact. Export therefore waits when necessary and never writes quick-view estimates.

Numeric construction is limited to two million nonzero output rows so it stays within
the transient-memory plan. Blank and missing renderer cells do not count toward that
limit. If a genuinely dense high-detail view exceeds the limit,
zoom in or choose a lower **Plot resolution** setting before exporting.

Select **Export image**, then choose PNG, SVG, or PDF in the native Save As dialog. All
three include the heatmap, coordinate axes, sequence labels, visible computed/imported
tracks, and a heatmap legend in a separate right margin for sketch plots (or a
categorical legend there for exact plots). PNG is a high-resolution raster. SVG and PDF
embed the heatmap as a raster but reconstruct axes, labels, tracks, and the legend as
vectors. For sketch plots, the legend scale is linear in `ANI_c`; its six evenly spaced ticks
divide the displayed range into five intervals. Its colors use the
same selected palette classes, color count, direction, custom colors, and
low/midpoint/high mapping shown by the plot, but that adjustable midpoint is not a
special legend tick. The palette name is not repeated beneath the scale.

Terminal exact plots use categorical legends rather than an `ANI_c` scale. **Identity**
labels the exact-match palette color; **Bases** lists the A/C/G/T colors; and Direction
lists forward, reverse, and neutral orientation. The selected plot background covers
mismatch/below-threshold positions and cells without supporting k-mer evidence; the
obsolete separate exact-state key is not included.

Chrome and Edge open the native system save picker, where the suggested filename and
format remain editable. The application asks the native picker to begin in Downloads,
although the browser may honor a previously used location instead.
Browsers without that API use their normal download behavior: the default BEDPE or PNG
format is written to the configured download location. Default filenames use the same
source-qualified identifiers shown in the sequence selectors.

Chrome may add security text such as “this site can see edits you make” to its native
file-system picker. That notice is owned by the browser and cannot be removed or styled
by ModDotPlot Browser. After the picker closes, a modal progress dialog blocks interaction
and reports detailed-tile preparation, image rendering, and file writing until the save
has completed.

Data and image files include machine-readable provenance for the software version, method,
scheduler policy, comparison parameters, complete scientific configurations, palette,
palette color count, direction, resolved ordered colors, display range, viewport, and
selected sequences. PNG provenance is stored in an
`iTXt` chunk; BEDPE/CSV use a JSON preamble; SVG uses `<metadata>`; PDF uses document
metadata.

## Sequence feature tracks

Feature tracks apply to a single interactive Self or Pairwise comparison and are
unavailable while Grid mode is active. Click a grid cell before enabling, importing,
or arranging tracks for that comparison.

Open **Feature tracks** to enable GC% or CpG observed/expected independently on either
axis. Annotation files staged on the launch screen enter the same import pipeline after
**Explore** is selected and the first interactive plot tile is available, so they do
not delay initial sequence display; annotation-only input never enables **Explore**.
Additional annotations can still be imported from the workspace. **Both** switches the
corresponding X and Y tracks together. Each enabled track
adds one thin row above the plot or one thin column to its left. Horizontal bars extend
upward and vertical bars extend leftward, away from the plot. Multiple tracks stack
outward while the square dotplot resizes to keep the page inside the browser window.

Each bar is calculated from the genomic window represented by that display column or
row; the values are not smoothed. GC% excludes ambiguous bases from its denominator.
CpG observed/expected uses `CpG × N / (C × G)` for canonical bases in the window and is
displayed on a 0–2 scale, with larger values clipped to the full track height.

Track data is computed locally on demand. The browser retains an overscanned region so
bars move immediately with ordinary panning. If a pan or zoom leaves that cache, the
track becomes blank immediately and is repainted only after a matching region has been
calculated, preventing an old track from appearing beside a new plot position.

Hover over a GC% or CpG bar to see its value and genomic window.

### Imported annotations

Drop a BED, GFF3, or GTF file on the X or Y coordinate axis, or use **Add track** at
the bottom of the Feature tracks panel. Plain-text, gzip, and BGZF versions are
accepted. An axis is highlighted while it is a valid drop target. File drops elsewhere
in the application are intercepted and reported instead of opening the file in the
browser. One file may contain at most 512 MiB of compressed or uncompressed input and
one million records matching the selected sequence. Larger imports are rejected with
an explanation before an unbounded completed-track graph can be retained.

Files staged on the landing screen or selected through **Add track** are scanned
against all loaded FASTA sequences. The browser merges the per-chromosome instances of
each logical annotation track into one sidebar row. Features are partitioned by
annotation sequence identifier, and the logical row automatically selects the
partition matching the FASTA sequence on each displayed axis. A file such as
`ColCEN_CEN180.gff3`, with
records for Chr1 through Chr5, therefore appears once rather than as five separately
deletable rows. GFF3 and GTF files naturally use the filename as their logical track
name. A BED file may still create multiple rows when it explicitly defines distinct
`track name=` datasets; same-named datasets are merged across matching chromosomes.

Changing an X or Y sequence makes the same logical row follow the newly matching
chromosome. The X, Y, and Both settings apply to the logical row as a whole and render
only when that axis's current sequence has mapped data. Batch imports start on Both;
an axis control is unavailable when the logical track has no matching records for its
current sequence. The row summary reports the number of matching sequences and the
combined displayed-feature count; deleting it removes all of its per-sequence data.
Dropping a file directly on an X or Y coordinate axis remains an explicitly scoped
single-sequence import; use **Add track** when one logical row should follow all
matching chromosomes.

Parsing occurs locally in a separate browser worker. Successful imports appear
immediately without a confirmation dialog. Import failures open a dialog with
validation and representative parsing errors. Exact sequence identifiers are
preferred. A conservative chromosome alias such as `1` and `chr1` must be confirmed.
Identifiers that match none of the loaded FASTA records do not create extra track
entries or appear on a displayed axis.

BED3–12 is supported, including UCSC `itemRgb`, thick regions, and BED12 blocks. GFF3
and GTF parent relationships are grouped into transcript models: exons are boxes,
CDS intervals are slightly taller boxes, introns are connecting sticks, and strand
direction is marked along the model. Protein-coding models are dark blue, pseudogenes
medium blue, RNA models green, and unclassified models dark gray. Hover a feature for
its name, type, coordinates, strand, and source details. Labels are not drawn
permanently so tracks remain thin.

Each imported track starts with one display row. Use its **− / +** control to select up
to ten deterministic packing rows; overlaps beyond the selected count share the last
row. Click and hold a visible track, then drag it over another track to reorder them. A
floating preview follows the pointer and the cursor changes from an open to a closed
hand. Dragging it outside the track strip, including over the dotplot, crosshatches the
entire preview; releasing disables that axis copy without deleting the parsed data.
Re-enable it with its X/Y checkbox. **Delete** in the control panel removes that track's
parsed data.

Y-axis coordinate labels are rotated to conserve horizontal space. Vertical feature
track labels are oriented with the bottom of the text toward the plot and placed at the
lower-coordinate end, matching the horizontal-track label convention.

## Progress and memory

The status and its small progress donut appear at the top of the control panel and show
progress for the current foreground work, including eager FASTA reading and validation,
on-demand indexed-record loading, and on-demand feature indexing.
The quick viewport is always completed and painted before detailed construction begins.
Detailed tiles then replace quick tiles individually as compatible detailed axis blocks
finish; the application does not wait for the complete detailed matrix.

The compact memory value at the bottom of the control panel estimates packed sequence
storage, Wasm structures, tile
arrays, and graphics textures. It does not include every byte owned by the browser or
graphics driver. Caches have bounded least-recently-used policies, but the current
overview and visible fallback tiles are protected and can temporarily exceed their
nominal budgets.

WebAssembly memory normally remains at its session high-water allocation even after
objects are discarded, although that space can be reused. Use **Clear** to remove live
application data. Reload the page to recreate the Wasm instance and fully reset the
browser session.

## Privacy and persistence

ModDotPlot Browser does not intentionally transmit loaded sequence or feature-file bytes,
and it contains no analytics or application server API. The static hosting provider
can still observe ordinary page and asset requests, and browser extensions operate
outside the application's control. See [Privacy and local data handling](PRIVACY.md).

Sessions are not persisted. Reloading or closing the tab discards the application
state. Keep your source FASTA files available if you need to recreate a view.

## Current limitations

* v0.9.3 remains a functional preview. Existing bounded estimator evidence is not a
  universal guarantee. Clean-Git packaging, reproducibility, and tagging remain a
  repository-owner step for this source-archive checkpoint.
* Very large records are limited by available browser memory; bounded in-memory
  sharding and indexed on-demand loading are implemented, but optional disk spill may
  still be needed before claiming robust 1 Gb operation across ordinary laptops.
* Identity estimates below roughly 80% are not a target operating regime and are shown
  using the plot background by default.
* Export captures the current viewport after all intersecting tiles reach detailed or
  terminal exact quality. This can require additional computation before saving.

For implementation evidence and open validation work, see
[Implementation status](STATUS.md).

## Troubleshooting

### The application does not open from a downloaded folder

Serve the production directory through an HTTP server. Developers can run the Vite
development server as described in the [README](../README.md).

### A compressed FASTA is rejected

Confirm that the bytes are gzip or BGZF compatible and that the browser is current.
Indexed compressed access requires BGZF together with both matching `.fai` and `.gzi`
files; ordinary gzip is valid but is read eagerly. Verify companion filenames if an
index error identifies an orphan or malformed file.
For a memory-budget error, load a chromosome, haplotype, or smaller record subset; an
uncompressed copy contains the same packed sequence payload and will not avoid that
limit.

### Navigation becomes slow after extensive use

Wait for active work to finish, reduce Plot resolution or register counts, or choose
**Clear** and reload the input. Reload the page if you also need to release the Wasm
linear-memory high-water allocation.

### The plot is empty

The rotating helix means plot work is still underway. If it disappears and the plot
remains blank, confirm that both axis records are selected, then reset the view. An
honestly blank plot can also mean that the sequences have no detectable k-mer
containment above the current heatmap minimum.
